abertura: In the call you are about to hear, two people from the buyer's side are talking to each other. You are on the line, and you have not spoken yet.
Mark the three statements that are true of that situation.

itens.t: The most important information is often said in passing, not announced.
If you look lost, they will slow down.
Asking for a figure again tells them you are following.
Waiting until the end is the polite way to say you missed something.
A condition can be stated without ever being called a condition.
Anything that matters will be repeated later.

sec1.rationale: Nobody in that call is monitoring whether you are following. They cannot see you, and it is not their job. The one signal that works is the one you send: a question, at the moment you lose the thread.

nota.texto: You said that if you could fix one thing, it would be understanding what people are saying. This lesson is that — but the product is not comprehension. It is what you do in the second where comprehension fails.

abertura: Choose the better reading for each expression. You will use all six live, in class.

itens.t: Sorry, can you go back to…?
alts: I am naming the part I missed
I am asking you to start again
itens.ok: I am naming the part I missed

itens.t: Could you say that number again?
alts: I want that one figure, not the sentence around it
I did not understand anything you said
itens.ok: I want that one figure, not the sentence around it

itens.t: Do you mean X or Y?
alts: I understood enough to narrow it to two
I understood nothing
itens.ok: I understood enough to narrow it to two

itens.t: Just to check I got that: you said…
alts: I am confirming before I act on it
I am doubting what you said
itens.ok: I am confirming before I act on it

itens.t: Before you move on — the part about…
alts: I am stopping you at a specific place
I am interrupting because I am impatient
itens.ok: I am stopping you at a specific place

itens.t: Sorry?
alts: they repeat whatever they think mattered
they repeat exactly what I missed
itens.ok: they repeat whatever they think mattered

nota.titulo: Five of these are precise, one is not
nota.texto: Sorry? is the one everybody uses and the weakest of the six: it hands the choice of what to repeat back to the other person. The other five name the gap, and you get back exactly the piece you lost.

doc.texto:
Mark: So, on the Brazil one. I looked at the numbers last night. Recurring is somewhere around forty percent, which is lower than the two we saw in Mexico, but the retention is better. Peter, do you have the churn figure?

Peter: I have six point four percent annual, but that is from their own deck, so take it as directional. The thing I keep coming back to is delivery. If we fold them in, half of that delivery team is talking to our clients directly within a year.

Mark: Right, and that is the piece I want to hear from him on. Not whether they can do it. Whether they have done it. And look, if the answer is no, that is fine. It changes the price and it changes the timeline. It does not change whether we do this.

Peter: Agreed. One more thing before he joins. We should be clear that we are talking about a minority position first. Anything else and we spend six months on a structure nobody wants.

abertura: Each line below comes from the call. What is it?

itens.t: “Recurring is somewhere around forty percent.”
itens.ok: a figure

itens.t: “Six point four percent annual, but that is from their own deck.”
itens.ok: a figure

itens.t: “If the answer is no, it changes the price and the timeline.”
itens.ok: a condition

itens.t: “It does not change whether we do this.”
itens.ok: a decision

itens.t: “The thing I keep coming back to is delivery.”
itens.ok: an opinion

itens.t: “We are talking about a minority position first.”
itens.ok: a decision

nota.titulo: The one that is worth the most
nota.texto: “It changes the price and the timeline — it does not change whether we do this” is a condition, and nobody calls it one. It tells you that the honest answer costs you money and time, and not the deal. That is the single most useful thing said in those ninety seconds.

abertura: Mark the three statements that are true of the call.

itens.t: They compare the company to two others they have already looked at.
The churn figure comes from an independent source.
They want to hear whether the team has already delivered in English, not whether it could.
A no on English delivery ends the deal.
They have decided to open with a minority position.
They plan to spend six months on the structure.

sec4.rationale: Two of the four false statements are the comfortable readings: that the figures are solid, and that a no would be fatal. Neither is what was said.

nota.texto: Not whether they can do it — whether they have done it. That distinction is the whole question they will put to you, and the answer they are prepared to hear is the true one.

abertura: Something specific was missed. Choose the repair that gets that thing back.

itens.t: You missed the churn figure.
alts: Could you say that number again?
Sorry, I did not understand.
Can you repeat the whole thing?
itens.ok: Could you say that number again?

itens.t: You are not sure if forty percent was recurring revenue or retention.
alts: Do you mean recurring revenue, or retention?
Sorry?
I did not catch that part.
itens.ok: Do you mean recurring revenue, or retention?

itens.t: You want to be sure that a no does not end the conversation.
alts: Just to check I got that: a no changes the price, not the deal?
So it is fine either way?
Are you saying it is not a problem?
itens.ok: Just to check I got that: a no changes the price, not the deal?

itens.t: They are moving on and you still have a question about delivery.
alts: Before you move on — the part about delivery.
Wait, please.
I have a question at the end.
itens.ok: Before you move on — the part about delivery.

itens.t: You lost the last sentence completely.
alts: Sorry, can you go back to what you said about the structure?
Sorry?
Say again?
itens.ok: Sorry, can you go back to what you said about the structure?

nota.titulo: The repair is a sentence, not a noise
nota.texto: Every option on the right of these is understandable English. The one that works names the missing piece — and that is the difference between getting your figure back and getting a summary you did not need.

nota.titulo: These are the five you will say out loud in class
nota.texto: Under pressure nobody composes a new sentence — you recover one you already have. Writing them once is what makes them come out at the right second.

cl2.prompt: Two of these get you the missing piece back. Which two?

itens.t: “Sorry?”
“Could you say that number again? The churn one.”
“I did not understand. Can you repeat everything?”
“Just to check I got that: a no changes the price, not the deal?”

cl2.rationale: The two that work say which piece is missing. The two that do not hand the choice back to the other person — and they will repeat what they think mattered, which is rarely the part you lost.

callout.texto: “It changes the price and the timeline. It does not change whether we do this.” Conditions like that are almost never announced. Catching one is worth more than catching every figure in the call.

abertura: Write the four repairs you would have used on your last real call in English — one line each.

callout.texto: A repair works because it is ready, not because it is clever. Four written lines cover almost everything that goes missing on a call: a figure, a name, a condition, and a whole sentence.

abertura: Two places where you can hear people repairing constantly, and doing it well.

itens.texto: Listen to the interviewer, not only the founder: he checks and re-asks constantly, and nobody hears it as a failure to understand.
Two hosts taking apart real acquisitions, at length. The vocabulary is the one from your own conversations, and the pace is fast — which is the point.
